meta.title: Driver liability and fines
meta.summary: You will learn the main fines for breaking the Rules under the CAO, the penalties for driving while intoxicated and for leaving the scene of an accident, and what a driver must do after an accident. Amounts are given at an MCI of 4 325 tenge (2026)

p: Fines in the CAO are not given in tenge, but in monthly calculation indices (MCI). The MCI changes every year, and the amounts change with it. In 2026, 1 MCI = 4 325 tenge.

If you admit the offence and do not dispute it, you can pay 50% of the fine within 7 days, and if a camera recorded the offence, within 7 days of the notice being delivered ⟦18⟧. The discount is available only when the penalty under the article is a fine (or a warning). If the article allows disqualification from driving or arrest, there is no discount (CAO art. 810).
A repeat offence within a year of being punished almost always costs more. So one “minor” offence can cost twice as much next time.

There is no penalty points system in the law yet. In spring 2026 it was piloted in Astana, Almaty and Shymkent with no real penalties (20 points in a year would mean disqualification from driving), and the law on this is still only being drafted.

lesson.h: Table of fines: speed and common offences
list: Speeding by 10-20 km/h - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), CAO art. 592(1)
Speeding by 20-40 km/h - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 592(2)
Speeding by 40-60 km/h - 20 MCI (86 500 tenge), CAO art. 592(3)
Speeding by more than 60 km/h - 40 MCI (173 000 tenge), CAO art. 592(3-1); a repeat offence within a year - 60 MCI (259 500 tenge), CAO art. 592(5)
A repeat offence within a year of speeding by 20-60 km/h - 30 MCI (129 750 tenge), CAO art. 592(4)
Using a phone at the wheel other than through headphones or a hands-free system - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), a repeat offence 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 591
Not wearing a fastened seat belt or motorcycle helmet - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), CAO art. 593(2)
A child under 12 without a child restraint or other means of fastening them with a seat belt ⟦19⟧ - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), a repeat offence 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 593(1, 3)
Passengers outside the cabin, leaning out of windows and hatches, or doors open while moving - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 593(1-2)
Driving through a prohibiting traffic light signal or a traffic controller's prohibiting signal - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), a repeat offence 15 MCI (64 875 tenge), CAO art. 599
Failing to give way to a pedestrian - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), a repeat offence 15 MCI (64 875 tenge), CAO art. 600
Failing to give way to a vehicle with priority - 15 MCI (64 875 tenge), a repeat offence 20 MCI (86 500 tenge), CAO art. 594(2, 5) and art. 595(3, 4)
Breaking the rules on stopping or parking - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), on the pavement - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), in places for persons with disabilities - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 597
lesson.tip: The speed scale: 5, 10, 20 and 40 MCI. The bigger the excess, the more it costs.

list: Failing to give way to an emergency service vehicle with its beacon and siren on - 20 MCI (86 500 tenge), a repeat offence 40 MCI (173 000 tenge) or community service for 20 hours, CAO art. 598
Driving on the shoulder, pavement or footpath - 15 MCI (64 875 tenge), CAO art. 596(1)
Crossing an organised convoy or taking a place in it - 15 MCI (64 875 tenge), CAO art. 596(2)
Failing to comply with signs and markings (where no separate article applies) - 3 MCI (12 975 tenge), a repeat offence 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 601

Failing to switch on hazard warning lights or to put out a warning triangle, or breaking the rules on using headlights during the hours of darkness - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), a repeat offence 7 MCI (30 275 tenge), CAO art. 602(1-1, 3)
Creating a hazardous situation - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), a repeat offence - disqualification from driving for 6 months, CAO art. 606
Driving onto a level crossing with the barrier down or on a prohibiting signal - 20 MCI (86 500 tenge), a repeat offence - disqualification from driving for 6 months, CAO art. 607
No OGPO policy - 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 230(2); not passing the technical inspection - 5 MCI (21 625 tenge), CAO art. 590(9)

Breaking the Rules by a pedestrian or an e-scooter rider (for example, riding an e-scooter on the pavement after 25.08.2026) - 2 MCI (8 650 tenge), a repeat offence 10 MCI (43 250 tenge), CAO art. 615(1, 3)

p: The most dangerous offences are not punished with money alone. A court can disqualify a driver from driving or impose administrative arrest.
list: Driving onto the oncoming lane where this is prohibited - disqualification from driving for 6 months, or for 9 months if it causes material damage, CAO art. 596(3, 4-1)
An accident caused by you with damage to vehicles - 20 MCI (86 500 tenge), or with minor harm to health - 40 MCI (173 000 tenge) or disqualification from driving for up to 9 months, CAO art. 610
Driving with no licence or without the right category - 20 MCI (86 500 tenge); letting such a person drive - 50 MCI (216 250 tenge), CAO art. 612
Driving a car while disqualified from driving - 50 MCI (216 250 tenge) or arrest for 10 days, CAO art. 612(3)

Leaving the scene of an accident you were involved in - 50 MCI (216 250 tenge) or disqualification from driving for 1 year, CAO art. 611(2); without a licence - 100 MCI (432 500 tenge) or arrest for 30 days, CAO art. 611(3)
Failing to comply with a lawful police requirement to stop - 40 MCI (173 000 tenge) or arrest for up to 3 days, CAO art. 613(1)

Driving while intoxicated, or letting an intoxicated person drive - arrest for 15 days and disqualification from driving for 7 years, CAO art. 608(1); if it causes damage or minor harm - arrest for 20 days and disqualification for 7 years, CAO art. 608(3); without a licence - arrest for 20 days, CAO art. 608(6)
Repeat driving while intoxicated - arrest for 20 days and disqualification from driving for 8 years, CAO art. 608(3-1)

Refusing a test for intoxication - arrest for 15 days and disqualification from driving for 8 years, CAO art. 613(4); a repeat offence - arrest for 20 days and disqualification for 9 years, CAO art. 613(5)

lesson.h: Alcohol: there is no permitted limit
p: The Rules prohibit driving while intoxicated ⟦20⟧ and letting an intoxicated person drive ⟦21⟧.

The permitted per mille limit was removed from the medical examination rules back in 2020. In 2026, the Ministry of Health proposed setting a limit of 0.3 per mille, but the draft was sent back for revision, and as of summer 2026 it has not been adopted. A breathalyser reading is only an initial indicator: intoxication is established by a medical examination.
Refusing a test for intoxication is not a way out: for a refusal, drivers are disqualified for even longer than for intoxication itself (8 years against 7).

From 25 August 2026, if a criminal case for driving while intoxicated is discontinued on non-exonerating grounds (for example, an amnesty or the expiry of a limitation period), the right to drive is terminated all the same. It can be restored no sooner than after 8 years, following a medical examination and a test on the Rules (Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 326-VIII of 24.06.2026).
lesson.tip: The safest rule: if you have been drinking, do not get behind the wheel at all.

p: A driver must stop at the request of a police officer or a transport control officer in uniform ⟦22⟧. You must not leave the car without the officer's permission ⟦23⟧: this carries 5 MCI (CAO art. 613(12)).

On request, hand over your driving licence and the vehicle's documents for inspection, and, if you are carrying goods, the waybill and the documents for the goods ⟦24⟧. You do not need to carry a Kazakhstani driving licence if you have an identity document with you, and you do not need to carry a Kazakhstani vehicle registration certificate at all. On the officer's request you must take a test for intoxication ⟦25⟧, and you must not drink alcohol before it ⟦26⟧.

The officer who has stopped the car must come up to it without delay, explain the reason for the stop, and, if you ask, show their warrant card without handing it to you ⟦27⟧. From 12.07.2026, para. 7 has been supplemented: if the offence was recorded by certified special technical devices, the officer shows the driver these materials for them to review.
A driver must also make their car available to medics and the police for the urgent transport of a person to hospital ⟦28⟧.

lesson.h: What to do after a road accident ⟦29⟧
list: Stop immediately and do not move the car
Switch on the hazard warning lights and put out a warning triangle: not closer than 15 m in a built-up area and 30 m outside it ⟦30⟧
Do not move objects relating to the accident

Give the injured first aid and call an ambulance. In an emergency, send the casualty in a passing vehicle, and if that is not possible, take them to the nearest hospital in your own car, give your name and vehicle number there, and return to the scene

Report it to the police without delay, write down the names and addresses of witnesses, and wait for police officers. Exceptions ⟦31⟧: if nobody is injured and the drivers agree, you may draw up and sign a sketch and go to the nearest police unit, and with simplified documentation you may manage without the police at all

If other vehicles cannot get past, clear the carriageway, but first record the position of the vehicles, the marks and the objects in front of witnesses, and make sure the scene of the accident can be driven around
lesson.tip: The order: stop, hazard lights, the triangle, help the people, call the police.

lesson.h: What you must not do after an accident
p: You must not leave the scene of an accident you were involved in. This is a separate offence: 50 MCI or disqualification from driving for 1 year ⟦32⟧.

You must not consume alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances after an accident you are involved in, until a test for intoxication has been carried out or an authorised person has decided that it is not needed ⟦33⟧. “A drink to calm down” is a straightforward violation.

lesson.h: Documenting an accident without the police
p: The Rules recognise the concept of “simplified documentation of an accident” - completing the documents without police officers in the cases established by the law on compulsory insurance of the liability of vehicle owners (OGPO).

An accident can be documented this way only if all the conditions are met. This is done through a mobile app: you fill in a declaration and attach photos and video. You may leave only after the insurer confirms that the declaration has been accepted.
list: Exactly two vehicles are involved
Both drivers have a valid OGPO policy
The estimated cost of repairs is no more than 100 MCI (432 500 tenge in 2026)
There is no dispute about who is at fault or about the list of damage
Nobody is injured, and only the vehicles are damaged (not poles, kerbs or barriers)
You may leave only after being notified that the insurer has accepted the declaration

keyFacts: In 2026, 1 MCI = 4 325 tenge (Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan on the Republican Budget for 2026-2028)
Speeding: by 10-20 km/h - 5 MCI, by 20-40 - 10 MCI, by 40-60 - 20 MCI, by more than 60 - 40 MCI ⟦1⟧
Admit the offence and pay within 7 days - you pay 50% of the fine ⟦2⟧
Driving while intoxicated - arrest for 15 days and disqualification from driving for 7 years ⟦3⟧
Refusing a test for intoxication - arrest for 15 days and disqualification from driving for 8 years ⟦4⟧
Leaving the scene of an accident - 50 MCI or disqualification from driving for 1 year ⟦5⟧
There is no permitted per mille limit in the Rules; a limit of 0.3 per mille was only proposed ⟦6⟧
After an accident: stop, do not move the car, switch on the hazard lights, put out the triangle, do not move objects ⟦7⟧
A warning triangle is put out not closer than 15 m in a built-up area and 30 m outside it ⟦8⟧
After an accident you must not drink alcohol until a test for intoxication or a decision to waive it ⟦9⟧
Without the police: two vehicles, OGPO for both, repairs up to 100 MCI, nobody injured and no dispute (the OGPO Act)
Failing to give way to a vehicle with its beacon and siren on - 20 MCI, a repeat offence 40 MCI or community service ⟦10⟧
mistakes: “0.3 per mille is already allowed.” No: the limit was only proposed, and the Rules have no permitted level. For intoxication - arrest and disqualification from driving for 7 years ⟦11⟧.

“After a minor accident you can just drive off if you have agreed.” You cannot. If nobody is injured and the drivers agree, they may draw up and sign a sketch and go to the police together ⟦12⟧, or document the accident the simplified way through the insurer. Simply driving off is leaving the scene of an accident ⟦13⟧.

“After an accident, you must roll the car onto the shoulder straight away.” At first, it is not moved at all. The carriageway is cleared only if other vehicles cannot get past, and only after the position of the car has been recorded in front of witnesses ⟦14⟧.
“I can have a drink after the accident, I am not driving any more anyway.” You must not, until a test for intoxication or a decision to waive it ⟦15⟧.
“It is better to refuse the test for intoxication.” For a refusal, drivers are disqualified for 8 years, which is even longer than for intoxication itself ⟦16⟧.
“A camera fine can be paid at a discount at any time.” The 50% discount applies only for 7 days from the day the notice is delivered ⟦17⟧.
